**Root cause analysis and current status**

The publisher uses git history to determine which files changed in the latest commit (when `COMMIT_ID` is set). If APIM-resource folders are **deleted** in a commit, the publisher should pick up those deletions and remove the resources from APIM.

There are two common reasons why deletions may not work:

1. **`COMMIT_ID` is not being passed to the publisher** — Without a `COMMIT_ID`, the publisher falls back to publishing everything currently in the artifacts folder. Since the deleted folder is gone, the publisher sees nothing to delete and nothing to add for those APIs — so APIM is left unchanged. PR [#233](https://github.com/lucabol/JediTestRepoV2/pull/233) adds a `WARN` log message when the publisher runs without `COMMIT_ID` to make this scenario more visible.

2. **Shallow git checkout (`fetch-depth: 2`)** — The GitHub Actions checkout in `run-publisher-with-env.yaml` currently uses `fetch-depth: 2`. If there is a merge commit at HEAD, the diff against the parent may not include files from the merged feature branch. PR [#134](https://github.com/lucabol/JediTestRepoV2/pull/134) changes this to `fetch-depth: 0` (full history) to reliably capture all changed/deleted files.

**Suggested workaround while the PRs are pending review:**
Update `tools/github_workflows/run-publisher-with-env.yaml` in your repo to use `fetch-depth: 0`, and ensure `COMMIT_ID` is correctly passed from the `get-commit` job's output (`${{ needs.get-commit.outputs.commit_id }}`).
